valuation_philosophy: FSF.NZ is a unit trust holding 'Economic Rights' over Fonterra Co-operative Group shares. A unit carries the SAME economic entitlement (dividends and capital returns) as one Fonterra farmer-share, but NO voting rights and NO governance influence. A conventional group-FCF DCF is the WRONG model for this instrument: Fonterra's dominant cost line is the Farmgate Milk Price paid to farmer-suppliers ($10.16/kgMS = ~$15.3bn in FY2025, against group revenue of ~$22-26bn), and the co-operative's board and governance structure are explicitly obligated to maximise that price for farmer-owners, NOT to maximise group profit or free cash flow available to Fund unit holders. Group FCF is therefore not a cash flow unit holders have any claim on or influence over -- it is structurally routed to milk suppliers and to retained capital at the co-operative's discretion. The ONLY cash a unit holder ever actually receives is (a) the declared per-unit dividend and (b) occasional capital returns. This model is accordingly built as a DIVIDEND DISCOUNT MODEL: projected dividends per unit are discounted at a cost of equity that is loaded with structural premiums specific to this instrument (no vote / co-op conflict of interest, Fund-size-cap and delisting/wind-up risk, dairy commodity cyclicality), with a terminal value from a terminal dividend (Gordon growth) capped by a historical exit P/E multiple on terminal EPS. Net debt is NOT subtracted from the DDM value -- dividends are already a post-interest, post-capital-structure cash flow, so netting debt again would double-count leverage. The one-off NZ$2.00/unit tax-free capital return from the Mainland Group divestment was PAID on 14 April 2026 and is a COMPLETED past event, not a projected future cash flow; the current $7.05 price is already ex-that-distribution (price fell from ~$8.20 to ~$6.55 across April 2026 before partially recovering). It is explicitly excluded from this valuation.

structural_notes.instrument: Unit trust holding Economic Rights over Fonterra Co-operative Group Limited shares; no voting rights, no governance role
structural_notes.denominator_used: ~1.607 billion Fonterra shares (the economic base), NOT the Fund's 107.4 million units on issue -- one unit = one share's economic entitlement
structural_notes.mainland_divestment: Global Consumer business (Anchor, Mainland, Kapiti, Perfect Italiano, Western Star) sold to Lactalis for NZ$4.22bn, completed 31 March 2026. Fonterra is now a focused NZ Ingredients + Foodservice co-operative.
structural_notes.capital_return_completed: NZ$2.00/unit tax-free capital return (~NZ$3.2bn) PAID 14 April 2026, funded from Mainland sale proceeds. This is a PAST, completed cash flow -- current $7.05 price is already ex-this-distribution. NOT added to intrinsic value.
structural_notes.earnings_discontinuity: FY2026 EPS guidance 50-65c (raised from 45-65c) reflects the step-down in earnings from losing Mainland's contribution. Management targets a return to pre-divestment ("current") group earnings levels within approximately 3 years (~FY2028/29). Historical FY2023-25 revenue/EPS trend is NOT extrapolated through this discontinuity.
structural_notes.net_debt_treatment: Net debt is NOT subtracted from the DDM valuation. Two net-debt figures exist on different definitions: FY2025 'adjusted net debt' NZ$2.6bn (1.1x EBITDA, management's covenant basis) vs H1-2026 reported net debt NZ$4.9bn (down from NZ$5.5bn; includes leases/other, and reflects the post-capital-return balance sheet carrying more debt than the FY2025 adjusted figure implies). This is a definitional difference, not a real one-period deterioration. Since dividends are already paid out of a post-interest, post-capex, post-debt-service cash flow, subtracting net debt again in a DDM would double-count leverage that is already embedded in the dividend capacity.

cost_of_equity_build.premium_governance_rationale: No voting rights / no control; co-operative governance explicitly and structurally prioritises maximising the Farmgate Milk Price paid to farmer-suppliers over group profitability accruing to Fund unit holders -- a direct, unresolvable conflict of interest with no unit-holder recourse
cost_of_equity_build.premium_fund_structure_rationale: Fund-size cap cut from ~20% to 10% of Fonterra shares under 2023 Flexible Shareholding reform; voluntary ASX delisting Feb-2025; buy-out pricing formula de-linked from the (unlisted) internal farmer share price in 2024; a live, monitorable Fund wind-up/marginalisation risk even though management has stated 'no appetite at this stage' to wind it up entirely
cost_of_equity_build.premium_commodity_cyclicality_rationale: Dairy commodity (Global Dairy Trade) price cyclicality, Greater China demand concentration (~1/3 of NZ dairy export volume), weather/drought risk on NZ milk collection volumes
cost_of_equity_build.wacc_rationale: Built as 9.0% NZ equity base + 2.25% governance/no-vote premium + 1.25% Fund-structure/wind-up-risk premium + 1.25% commodity-cyclicality premium = 13.75% base-case cost of equity. This sits within the instructed 13-14% band. Bull case uses 12.75% (thesis de-risking as recovery executes); bear case uses 15.25% (structural risks crystallising).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Raw historical CAGRs are NOT used to drive this valuation and diverge enormously from each other and from the forward projection: dividend 5yr CAGR of 62.7% is a base-effect artefact of FY2020's near-zero 5c dividend recovering to 57c by FY2025, not a sustainable growth rate. EPS CAGRs are distorted by the FY2023 Soprole one-off gain (EPS 0.95 vs ~0.60-0.65 normalised) and by the FY2026 Mainland-divestment earnings step-down, which breaks any simple extrapolation. Revenue CAGR (8.7% 3yr) describes a group that has since sold ~15-20% of its earnings base (Mainland) and is therefore not forward-relevant either. selected_growth_rate is instead the terminal (steady-state, post-recovery) dividend growth rate used directly in the DDM Gordon-growth terminal value -- see assumptions.base.terminal_growth -- because this is a distribution-capitalisation model, not a historical-CAGR-extrapolation model.
historical_growth.note: Because Group FCF is not the relevant cash flow (see valuation_philosophy) and the FY2026 Mainland divestment breaks the historical earnings/revenue series, this DDM anchors forward dividends to FY2026 EPS guidance (50-65c midpoint) and management's explicit '~3 year earnings recovery' target rather than to trailing CAGRs.

base.eps_path_rationale: Y1 = FY2026 guidance midpoint (50-65c). Y2-Y3 recover toward management's ~3-year 'return to pre-divestment earnings' target (~70c). Y4-Y10 grow at a tapering rate (8.5% -> 1.75%) converging to terminal growth as the post-Mainland business matures.
base.payout_rationale: Starts modestly below FY2025's 80% (top-of-range) payout while the business rebuilds post-divestment, then normalises toward 75%, within the stated 60-80% policy band
base.terminal_exit_pe_cap_rationale: Average of clean historical P/E multiples FY2020, FY2021, FY2022, FY2024, FY2025 (8.88, 10.39, 8.39, 5.90, 10.43), excluding FY2023's Soprole-gain-distorted 3.72x and the loss-making FY2018/19 (n/m)

bull.eps_path_rationale: Y1 = top of FY2026 guidance (65c). Faster Foodservice/protein-led recovery (Q3 FY2026 Foodservice underlying operating profit +143% YoY cited as evidence) drives EPS to ~82c by Y3, above management's base target, then grows steadily.

bear.eps_path_rationale: Y1 below the bottom of FY2026 guidance range (50c) as milk price stays elevated ($9.40-10.00/kgMS guided) compressing Ingredients margin; minimal recovery thereafter as China demand and commodity cycle risks persist.
bear.terminal_exit_pe_cap_rationale: 10-year historical minimum P/E among profitable years (FY2024), excluding FY2018/19 loss years (n/m)

entry_price.methodology: Entry price = PV of base-case projected dividends (Y1-Y10) discounted at the 15% hurdle, plus PV of the base-case terminal value (computed at cost-of-equity/WACC for exit fairness, then discounted back at the 15% hurdle). No net-debt adjustment (DDM). This is the price at which buying today, collecting the projected dividend stream, and exiting at fair value in Year 10 earns a 15% IRR.

base.entry_vs_iv_note: Entry price sits modestly below intrinsic value ($3.93 vs $4.22), consistent with the 15% hurdle exceeding the 13.75% base-case cost of equity.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = cost of equity, Columns = terminal growth; base case is the center cell (13.75%, 1.75%) = $4.22

sanity_check.diagnosis: At $7.05, the market is pricing FSF at 12.3x FY2026 guided EPS (midpoint) -- ABOVE the 10-year historical maximum P/E ever achieved (10.43x, itself set in FY2025 after a large run-up) and 39% above the clean historical average of 8.8x. This is the OPPOSITE of a trip condition: the model's implied exit multiples (6.25x base, 7.44x bull, 4.56x bear) are all AT OR BELOW the historical average, meaning the DDM is not assuming any multiple expansion -- if anything it assumes reversion toward or below historical norms. No lever needed adjustment (cost of equity, payout, or terminal growth all sit within reasonable, well-documented bands). The conclusion that current price implies meaningful downside across all three scenarios (including bull, at -11.7%) is a function of the market currently paying a premium multiple for the post-divestment recovery/re-rating story, not a modelling error.

sanity_check.conclusion: No fix required. The valuation is internally consistent: all three scenarios' implied exit multiples sit at or below the company's own trading history, yet all three land below the current $7.05 price because the current price itself already trades above the historical multiple ceiling. This is read as the market pricing in the post-Mainland-divestment simplification/re-rating and 3-year earnings-recovery narrative ahead of it being delivered -- a legitimate but unproven bull thesis, not a valuation-model error.
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- model implies multiple contraction (6.25x exit vs 8.8x historical average), not expansion. Current price at 12.3x FY2026 guided EPS is above the 10yr historical max, which is a statement about the market, not the model.

conclusion.verdict: FSF.NZ units appear OVERVALUED at the current $7.05 price under this dividend discount model. Base case intrinsic value is $4.22/unit (-40% downside), probability-weighted intrinsic value $4.23/unit (-40%), and even the bull case ($6.22, -12%) sits below the current price. The current price implies a P/E of ~12.3x FY2026 guided EPS, above any multiple the co-operative's units have traded on in the last decade (historical range 5.9x-10.4x, excluding loss years and the Soprole-gain-distorted FY2023). This is not a business-quality criticism -- Fonterra's post-divestment deleveraging, Foodservice growth, and 10-12% ROC target are real positives reflected in the bull case -- but the structural realities of the instrument (no vote, co-operative conflict of interest over the Farmgate Milk Price, Fund-size-cap/wind-up risk) justify a cost of equity (13.75% base) high enough that even a successful 3-year earnings recovery does not clear the current price. A negative expected return at today's price is the honest conclusion of this model, not a modelling artefact.
